name: Act of February 19, 1873 to provide for the sale of certain New York Indian lands in Kansas (17 Stat. 466)
aka: Kansas lands of the New York Indians, Royce area 249
nations: Brothertown (the New York Indians of the 1838 Buffalo Creek treaty)
promises: The 1838 Treaty of Buffalo Creek (kappler-510) set apart 1,824,000 acres in what became Kansas as a permanent home for the New York Indians; certificates of allotment of 320 acres each were issued on September 14, 1860 to thirty-two of them.

The 1873 Act let settlers who occupied those allotted lands buy them, up to 160 acres each, at the appraised value and at no less than $3.75 an acre, with the money to be held in trust for the allottees or their heirs.
If an allottee or heir did not prove identity within five years of the Act, the unpaid proceeds were to pass to the public treasury.

breaches.what: Congress authorised settlers occupying the lands in Kansas allotted to thirty-two New York Indians under certificates of September 14, 1860 to enter and purchase them. The Act contains no provision for the allottees' consent; it held the purchase money in trust for them for five years only.

source.title: Act of February 19, 1873, ch. 167, 17 Stat. 466 (An Act to provide for the Sale of certain New York Indian Lands in Kansas)

breaches.quote: authorized and permitted to enter and purchase at the proper land-office said lands so occupied by them

breaches.what: The Supreme Court found that the Kansas lands promised by the 1838 treaty were surveyed, made part of the public domain and sold by the United States, which received the consideration, and ordered judgment for the net amount the government received for the Kansas lands. It also found that only thirty-two New York Indians received allotments there, 10,240 acres in all.

landTaken: The allotted lands were 320 acres each for thirty-two New York Indians, 10,240 acres in all (New York Indians v. United States, 1898). The whole Kansas tract was 1,824,000 acres.
compensation: The 1873 Act put sale money in trust for the allottees for five years. The 1898 Supreme Court judgment was for the net amount the government received for the Kansas lands, without interest, less deductions; the final figure was not confirmed (see kappler-510).
today: The Kansas lands are counted once, on kappler-510 (the 1838 Treaty of Buffalo Creek). A later Act of June 23, 1874 (18 Stat. 273) altered the terms of payment by settlers on the allotted lands (Royce p. 876).

nationVoice.summary: The Nation's archive calls the 1838 Buffalo Creek treaty, under which the Kansas lands were promised, fraudulently executed.

openQuestions: Same land as kappler-510 (Royce area 249, the Kansas tract of the 1838 treaty), so it is counted once there; sameEventAs points at kappler-510.

The lead given for this round (Emigrant New York Indians, ICC Docket 75, 177 Ct. Cl. 263) concerns the Green Bay, Wisconsin lands bought from the Menominee in 1822 and lost under the 1831-32 treaties, not the Kansas lands. The 1966 Court of Claims opinion was opened and mentions Kansas only as the 1838 exchange.
Whether the 1898 judgment's net amount included money from the 1873 sales of allotted land was not settled; the opinion speaks of the Kansas lands as a whole.
The rest of the Act (17 Stat. 467) was not read; the five-year clause is read from page 466 only, where the sentence continues onto the next page.
treaties.json lists no presentDayTribes and no statute link for this record; 17 Stat. 466 is the citation Royce gives. Not edited.

Audit 2026-11-08: 17 Stat. 466 read on govinfo (quote exact, line-broken as "per-mitted"). New York Indians v. United States, 170 U.S. 1 (April 11, 1898) re-read: it states the Kansas lands were surveyed, made part of the public domain and sold, the United States receiving the consideration, records 32 allotments of 320 acres (10,240 acres), and remands for judgment for the net amount received for the Kansas lands. sameEventAs kappler-510 kept: kappler-510 carries Royce area 249 and has a findings file. No change.

plain.promised: The 1838 Buffalo Creek treaty promised the New York Indians a permanent home in Kansas; thirty-two of them received 320-acre allotments there in 1860.
plain.happened: In 1873 Congress let settlers living on those allotments buy them, with no provision for the owners' consent. The Supreme Court found in 1898 that the United States sold the Kansas lands and kept the money.
plain.today: Counted once with the 1838 treaty. The Court ordered judgment for what the government received for the Kansas lands; the final figure was not confirmed.
